messages:
carlos-customer: Hey support — since last deploy our consumers started failing when using structured JSON mode. Parser errors: "Unexpected token at position 142". We set json_mode=per_item and pass a JSON schema for items. Request ID rid_abc123. Can someone look? This is blocking a release.

jess-support: Sorry about that — can you paste the request (redacting secrets) and the raw API response? Also which model + runtime (hosted/dedicated/private)?

carlos-customer: cURL and response (trimmed):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-open-1.3","json_mode":"per_item","json_schema": {"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","required":["id","text","metadata"]}} ,"input": "..."}'
```

Response body we got: (raw)

```json
[
  {"id": "msg-1", "text": "hello", "metadata": {"lang":"en"}},
  {"text": "missing id field", "metadata": {"lang":"en"}, "tmp": 42},
  {"id": "msg-3", "text": "ok", "metadata": null}
]
```

Notice: second item missing required `id`, contains extra key `tmp`. Third item has `metadata` null (schema required object). Our parser is strict and throws on first invalid item which breaks our pipeline. We did not change client side.

jess-support: Thanks — this looks like schema drift from model outputs (some items partial/nullable). Quick questions: were you streaming responses? Did you enable `stream=true`? Also did you see any retries/repeat requests around 2026-03-01T14:02Z (rid_abc123)?

carlos-customer: Yes streaming was on (stream=true). We saw many partial chunks and client retried on parse error which spiked token usage.

anya-eng: Looping in infra/ML — what likely happened: when streaming + per_item JSON, the runtime sometimes emits partially-constructed objects in separate chunks; our JSON-mode verifier accepts only complete per-item docs. However, there is a corner-case where model hallucinations or temperature changes can drop required fields or emit extra debug keys. With streaming enabled some mid-chunk partial items can be checkpointed and returned as complete array entries by older runtime versions.

anya-eng: Immediate workarounds:
- Turn off streaming (stream=false) so you receive final canonical output.
- Use json_mode: "single_document" with a top-level wrapper and run your own per-item validation after receipt.
- If you must stream, set client to buffer until each object's closing brace is observed (robust JSON reassembly).

jess-support: Also: server-side temporary mitigations we can apply — we can run a tolerant pre-processor that rejects items missing required keys instead of returning malformed items. I can enable that for your org for a short window while we triage. Want me to flip that?

carlos-customer: Please enable the tolerant filter. Also we need a repro for your eng team: I captured a full debug trace: rid_abc123, region: us-west-2, model variant: rwd-open-1.3-quant, runtime: hosted-v2. Attached logs (internal).

sre-oncall: We see an uptick in error rate for /v1/generate from that customer between 14:01–14:05 UTC. Retry storms increased tokens billed by ~2.9x. We'll throttle retries client-side by default for 429s and add guidance in docs.

billing-bot: Noted. If support confirms the malformed output is on our side and caused retry billing spike, we can issue a provisional credit. Please open a billing case with the attach and tag billing. Ticket: BILL-2026-784.

anya-eng: Root cause hypothesis: a regression in the streaming assembler in hosted-v2 that occasionally emits an item when the model produces an early end-of-item token (e.g., model injected "\n" inside nested object), which our JSON flattener mistakenly finalizes. Fix: patch streaming assembler to only finalize array items upon encountering an item-level boundary token sequence. We have a patch in review and will push to hosted-v2 tonight.

jess-support: For now I've enabled the tolerant pre-processor for your org (will suppress malformed items and return a 207 with per-item status when possible). I've also created internal issue RED-3921 and linked logs.

carlos-customer: Thanks — tolerant mode helps. Two asks: 1) ETA on runtime fix? 2) Can you confirm we won't be billed for retry storm until billing review?

anya-eng: ETA: patch merged -> canary deploy in 6 hours, global rollout in 24–48 hours depending on canary health.

billing-bot: We'll flag BILL-2026-784 for review; provisional credit is likely once engineering confirms malformed output caused the retries.

deploy-bot: deploy started for hosted-v2 patch RED-3921 to canary (canary group: 2%).

jess-support: I'll follow up in this thread with a postmortem when the patch completes and confirm billing outcome. In the meantime, keep stream=false where possible or rely on tolerant pre-processor. :thumbsup:
